title: Graphs of linear functions
summary: Plot and interpret straight-line graphs using points, intercepts, equations and intersections.
objectives: Generate points for a straight-line graph from its equation.
Find and interpret x- and y-intercepts.
Find equations and intersections of straight-line graphs.

sections.title: Generate accurate points for a straight-line graph

blocks.text: A point lies on a graph only if its coordinates satisfy the equation. Choose several convenient x-values, calculate the matching y-values, plot the ordered pairs using the axis scales, and draw one straight line through them. Two points determine a mathematical line, while a third point provides a useful accuracy check.
Use a ruler or a digital straight-line tool rather than joining points with separate short segments. Extend only across the shown or meaningful domain and label the line with its equation.
The y-intercept is where the graph crosses the y-axis, so x = 0. The x-intercept is where the graph crosses the x-axis, so y = 0. An intercept is a complete coordinate, not just one number.
For y = -2x + 8, the diagram shows the two intercepts (0, 8) and (4, 0). Substituting either coordinate into the equation gives a true statement.

sections.title: Interpret the intersection of two graphs

blocks.text: Two graphs intersect at an ordered pair that satisfies both equations. On a drawn graph, read both coordinates carefully from the scales. Algebraically, set the two expressions for y equal, solve for x, and substitute to find the shared y-value.

A graph gives an estimate when the intersection falls between grid lines; algebra gives an exact value when the equations are known. In a context, interpret both coordinates and reject intersections outside the meaningful domain.

sections.title: Worked example: find both coordinate-axis intercepts

prompt.text: For y = -2x + 8, find both coordinate-axis intercepts and use them to describe how to draw the graph.

content.text: Plot the two points and draw the straight line through them.

sections.verification_note: Both points satisfy y = -2x + 8. The graph falls from left to right, which agrees with the negative coefficient of x.

sections.title: Worked example: solve a graph intersection

prompt.text: Find the intersection of y = 2x + 1 and y = -x + 7.

content.text: At the intersection, both expressions have the same y-value.
Substitute into either equation to find y.

sections.verification_note: The point checks in the second equation because -2 + 7 = 5, so (2, 5) lies on both lines.

prompt.text: Find the x-coordinate where y = 3x - 12 crosses the x-axis.

feedback.text: At the x-axis y = 0, so 3x - 12 = 0 and x = 4.

blocks.text: Calculate and plot ordered pairs using the marked scales, use an additional point to check accuracy, and draw one labelled straight line through the valid domain.
Set x = 0 for the y-intercept and y = 0 for the x-intercept. At an intersection, equate the two expressions for y, find the shared point and verify it in both equations.
